touches.text: Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
A diagnostic report, EXACTLY like the Trouble Tickets in the Number Five Crossbar Telephone Switch. It MUST include EVERYTHING needed to diagnose, isolate, and repair the trouble.
The test before raising one: can only CC or Akien fix this? If not, it is a log line, not a trouble. One problem, one trouble.

A trouble ticket is a work order. Whoever fixed it reports the fix to the originator (the device or machine that raised it), and the originator marks it fixed. A trouble that comes back is not designed for yet; if recurrent problems appear, we'll explore that.
Trouble tickets (3.4.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.3.7.1.3).
Trouble: it has to be able to report when nothing else can, so a direct line makes sense for recovery (6.3.4).
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).

The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien until the outline is implemented; a design agent comes after that. Until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.
Test tiers: commit, hourly, daily and weekly. Each tier runs only what it must, so a commit needs only its own proofs and the long runs wait for the long tiers; nothing runs just in case.
A second observation of an open trouble NEVER issues a new ticket; it increments a counter on the open one.
Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).

conflicts.text: Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.
conflicts.ticket_says: When a door refuses a red's ticket, the red is left new for the next run to try again, and an unticketed trouble is raised. 'Every run still tries to write the red's ticket...a refusal leaves the red new, so the next run tries again.'
conflicts.why: The outline states: 'Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds...unless one is already open.' The ticket implementation results in some runs NOT writing the ticket (when door refuses), only leaving it new for retry. The outline prescribes the write happens in each run; the ticket accepts some runs do not write. The door-refusal case is not an exception the outline names, so this violates the stated clause.

conflicts.text: Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
conflicts.ticket_says: When RedTicketRefused (cast door refuses), run_proof raises an unticketed trouble and emits red_unticketed. It does not write a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
conflicts.why: Outline 9.4.2.3.1 requires run_proof to 'write a validation record' but the ticket prevents this when a gate refuses, writing a trouble (diagnostic report) instead—a different record type with different structure.
